title: I highly recommend Space Aces: The New Guidebook - solo science fiction RPG
body:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=K8o_u0_iFJU

Daniel (@dungeondive) recommends Space Aces: The New Guidebook without reservation, a rules-light solo RPG of roughly 32 pages, 28 of them generators, that he reads as early-1980s anime in zine form: Dirty Pair, Crusher Joe, Space Adventure Cobra. You are mostly competent, heavily in debt and highly motivated, working gigs for a galactic agency. His crew is Sam Foyle and Angela Antella, a married couple paying off a gambling debt aboard the Star Sparrow, a fast, fragile ship with stylish uniforms and not enough legroom.

Nearly all the rules fit on the character sheet. Five stats (Moxie, Smarts, Wiggles, Friends, Pockets) add to a d20 against difficulties of 5, 10, 15 or 20, while a d6 complication die rolled alongside adds a cost, a standard result or a benefit regardless of success. Failures bank grit, five grit buys a success, and each cost pushes up a heat level that raises the stakes and doubles as a timer. Gumption stands in for hit points in the manner of a Saturday-morning cartoon: nobody dies, they just get knocked out of the scene.

He shows his running campaign, a search for a lost expedition on a roaming artificial planet that turns out to be a weapon, complete with a supernova, a rival crew called the Space Punks and a psionic stellar jellyfish, then builds a fresh mission live with the MacGuffin maker. Gaps he flags: no room-by-room generator for derelicts, so he leans on the Starforged reference guide, and loose fuel rules.

----

Space Aces fits nearly all its rules on the character sheet. How simple can a solo RPG get before it stops feeling like a game and becomes pure prompt?
